affected_records.statement: 14 tracked record files in this corpus name one of the three unverifiable Altium anchors. Each of them rests, for its hardware provenance, on a design file this repository cannot show, and each of them already carries that limitation itself. The count is stated so the size of the inherited limitation is visible; it is not a count of defects, because none of these records is wrong about its own limitation.

authority_and_independence.independence_statement: Authored by an AI agent that re-ran the searches itself rather than taking the finding on trust. That makes the finding reproducible, not independent: no hardware engineer confirmed it, no design source was consulted because none could be, and no board was inspected.

blockers.blocker: No Altium design source in this repository, at any commit of any branch
blockers.consequence: Nothing downstream of a schematic can be derived here: no net, no reference designator, no component placement, no BOM line.
blockers.evidence: git ls-tree -r --name-only 308028fb -- hardware/ returns exactly one path, hardware/README.md. git log --all --name-only --diff-filter=A -- '*.SchDoc' '*.PcbDoc' '*.PrjPcb' returns no output. git ls-tree -r --name-only 308028fb -- docs/hardware/ returns 166 tracked files, of which 93 are CSV tables and 26 are draw.io sources, and none of them is an Altium file.

blockers.blocker: The designs are hosted outside this repository
blockers.consequence: The board inventory in FB2-HW-HCB-000001 is a configuration baseline, not a design baseline. It says which board and which version; it cannot say what is on the board.
blockers.evidence: The release index hardware/README.md points every board at a per-release zip archive on https://iisb-foxbms.iisb.fraunhofer.de/foxbms/gen2/hardware/release. docs/hardware/design-resources.rst states that the design packages for the masters, interfaces and slaves are available from the project repository.

blockers.blocker: The format is proprietary CAD and out of reach for an offline corpus even if fetched
blockers.consequence: Obtaining the archives would not make the design verifiable by this corpus. The unblock is a tool, not only a download, and recording it as only a download would understate what is missing.
blockers.evidence: docs/hardware/design-resources.rst names Altium Designer as the tool required to open the schematic and layout files.

blockers.blocker: The three existing hardware anchors cannot be verified, and were already recorded as such
blockers.consequence: No new evidence can be produced for those anchors from here, and any record depending on them inherits an unverifiable provenance.
blockers.evidence: FB2-SRC-HW-000001, FB2-SRC-HW-000002 and FB2-SRC-HW-000003 each carry content_hash 'unresolved' and location.file_hash 'unresolved', with hash_status 'external_design_file_unverifiable_from_this_repository' and a hash_note recording the same search this record repeats. Their external_file values name .SchDoc paths in a separate repository.

expected_families.basis: The schematic sources are Altium .SchDoc files hosted in a separate repository. No .SchDoc file exists in the foxbms-2 working tree or in any commit of any branch.
The layout sources are Altium .PcbDoc files hosted externally. No .PcbDoc file exists in the foxbms-2 working tree or in any commit of any branch.

No bill of materials file is tracked in this repository for any board at any version. docs/hardware/design-resources.rst lists a BOM in Excel format as part of the assembly files inside the external design package, which is where this corpus's BOM would have to come from.
No component specification for any board is tracked here. The device data sheets that would carry component limits are not in this repository and are not vendor-neutral substitutes for them.

record_verbatim.gap_statement: HWE.3 expects schematics, a PCB layout, a bill of materials and component specifications. All four are absent from this corpus, and none of them can be authored from this repository, because the design sources they would be derived from are not in it. This record is the finding that says so, with the evidence, so that a reader encountering HWE.3 in the coverage plan finds a reason rather than a silence. It deliberately contains no board-level design content: there is none here to carry, and inventing a net, a reference designator, a component, a register, an offset, a mask or a base address would be fabrication, not documentation.
not_established_by_this_record: No schematic, layout, net, reference designator, component, register, offset, mask or base address.
No bill of materials, not even a partial or an inferred one.
No component specification and no device data sheet content.
No discharge of HWE.3. The process remains a gap and this record says so in its own standards mapping, with status gap.
No claim that the corpus's existing hardware records are wrong. They already carry the limitation; this record makes the population visible.
No human approval, no independence, no certification, no ASPICE capability level.

what_would_close_the_gap.then: Schematics, layout and BOM become derivable and HWE.3 can be authored as content rather than as a finding.
what_would_close_the_gap.unblock: The Altium design sources for the boards under consideration are placed under version control that this corpus can read, or exported to a documented neutral format.

what_would_close_the_gap.then: The exported or committed sources become machine-checkable rather than merely present, and a BOM can be re-derived and compared.
what_would_close_the_gap.unblock: A tool able to read the format is available to the corpus.

what_would_close_the_gap.then: Component specifications become derivable; without them the component family stays absent even if the design sources arrive.
what_would_close_the_gap.unblock: Component data sheets for the parts actually placed are available under terms that permit their use.

what_would_close_the_gap.note: This record does not estimate how long that takes, does not schedule it, and does not treat the gap as expected to close soon. It is blocked, not late.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-HW-HDD-000001` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
